findings.issue: The extra `CI=1 npm test` (ng test) run was treated as a success, but the harness recorded it as passing 0 tests; the agent never inspected the vitest output to confirm the unit spec actually ran and passed.
findings.suggestion: Read the tail of the test output (executed/passed counts) before claiming a suite is green, or skip the non-required suite entirely.

findings.issue: Three write-then-immediately-fix cycles: broken normalizeTeam condition, a stray `import { Store } from '@ngrx/store'` in a package with no ngrx, and a wrong CSS variable name — each caught only by its own re-read of the just-written file.
findings.suggestion: Review generated code (or compile after each write batch) before moving on; these slips cost ~3 turns.

findings.issue: Invoked `npm test -- --run` in app/, an unsupported flag for `ng test` in this setup ('Unknown argument: run'), a wasted call for a suite that wasn't part of the task.
findings.suggestion: Check `ng test --help` or simply avoid running suites outside the task's test command.

findings.issue: A multi-hunk edit failed because edits[1] used stale oldText (wrote `pageRoute` where the file has `route`); had to inspect the file and redo the edit in turn 27.
findings.suggestion: Re-read the exact target region before multi-hunk edits, or apply changes one hunk at a time.

findings.issue: Attempted to grep app/node_modules before realizing dependencies weren't installed, producing a failed command and an extra discovery turn.
findings.suggestion: Check for node_modules (or run the install) before inspecting installed type definitions.

findings.issue: Consulted the Angular CLI MCP best-practices tool but never read the available angular-developer skill (measured skillReads: 0), the designated guidance for feature work.
findings.suggestion: Load the matching skill file at the start of a feature task; it's cheaper than re-deriving conventions.

summary: A well-run session: the agent mapped the spec, tests and existing SSR architecture before coding, made the one genuinely hard design decision (cookie-backed team store for SSR/hydration parity) deliberately and correctly, and debugged its single test failure by reading the Playwright failure artifacts and fixing the root cause. The full acceptance suite (63 tests) was green after its last edit. The deductions are minor and self-inflicted: three sloppy first writes that needed immediate fixes, one stale-text edit miss, and an accepted-but-unverified unit-test run at the end.
